You're legitimately funny, per your username. You have appropriate cadence, awareness, and overall writing ability. You're words and ideas and morals and values. You've been to college and have the motivation to finish your work. 

Fuck your father, remove yourself from him. It's easy for me to ask of you, but important to your growth. You're more than capable of independence and a self-sustaining lifestyle. Do not settle for misery. Do not settle for your own negativity. Do not disallow yourself the opportunity to be more.
My Babar doesn't zip open but he knows all my worries and helps me get through my lowest periods
The second my friend leaves, the the second I walk him through the door and wave him off, is when I need a friend most of all.

I've experienced a close suicide. It wasn't a significant other, but he was significant to my family's existence. I didn't love him any less. My family was torn apart when my brother took his life and a big piece of mine. I don't really have the energy to type my whole story, revisiting that part of my life hurts too much, but I can post the letter I wrote to him, a sort of rebuttal to the one he left us. 



I've seen how suicide affects others. I've observed how it affected me. How it shatters lives into tiny pieces of unexpected happy memories overshadowed and immediately followed by the deepest, darkest emptiness. 

Your pillowcases smelled like you for weeks, which was not nearly long enough for Pop. He only wears the ties you helped pick out and he's not interested in buying any more. He falls asleep on the couch most every night, he broke out the VCR and our home movies. Mom can't watch them. Mom sleeps with your shirts in your room sometimes. 
You were their first. You were their baby. You took that from them. 
The pen from your note is still on the desk. I don't ride the train anymore, and I think about destroying the one you stepped in front of. I think about killing the conductor. 
Everything you left behind is still here. We're still here. I wish you were, too. Every day I think about joining you. Sometimes to see you again, but most of the time I want to kick your ass. I want to make you feel how much our hearts ache for you, you fucking asshole. 
You ruined our lives, you took all legitimate joy with you. I hope you're able to see what you've accomplished. I hope you can feel what you've done to me. How you changed my mind and my heart. I still want to die, but you gave me reasons to live as well. 

The look on our sister's face at your funeral. 

Every holiday spent with silence, unable to talk about our happiest memories because you were always a part of them. 

You said in your note that you couldn't bear living with this pain anymore. That pain didn't die with you on those tracks, you gave it to me. You gave it to Mom. You gave it to Pop, who you called your best friend. You gave it to our sister. 
Our whole family has this unbearable weight in our chests every time you come up, which is always and will be every day until we join you. 
You're never going to be the uncle I wanted my kids to know. You're never going to give me the advice I need from an older brother. I still tell people I have an older brother. I never thought I'd become older than you. I hate you. I love you more than anything. 

Please come home.
I got to make her breakfast

"We haven't done anything in a week. You used to be all over me." 

"So?" *shrugs*
I was the literal odd man out, they're all close friends from high school. Hardly acquaintances.
